subject: storytime
title: The Elves and the Shoemaker
about: The Brothers Grimm's tale of a poor shoemaker who finds his shoes finished every morning, and of the thank-you he and his wife make for the two tiny elves who did the work. First graders love the secret night-time helpers and the night-then-morning pattern, and the ending is a gentle lesson in saying thank you. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Tap, tap, tap like the elves, then ask how the shoemaker and his wife said thank you.

book.author: the Brothers Grimm (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Two tiny elves, a lot of shoes, and a big thank-you.

passage.text:
Once there was a kind shoemaker.
He and his wife were very poor.
One night, he had one last bit of leather.
It was just enough for one pair of shoes.
He cut it out and set it on his bench.
"I will make the shoes in the morning," he said.
Then he went to bed.
***
In the morning, he got a big surprise.
The shoes were all done!
Every stitch was neat and tiny.
A man came in and bought them.
He paid a lot of money.
Now the shoemaker could get leather for two pairs.
That night, he cut it out and went to bed.
In the morning, two pairs of shoes were done!
***
This went on, night after night.
Soon they were not poor at all.
"Who is making our shoes?" asked his wife.
"Let's hide and see," said the shoemaker.
At midnight, two little elves came in.
They had no warm clothes.
Tap, tap, tap went their tiny hammers.
They made shoes all night long.
Then they ran out into the cold.
***
"The elves helped us," said the wife.
"But they looked so cold."
"Let's make them warm clothes to say thank you."
She made two tiny shirts and two tiny coats.
He made two pairs of tiny shoes.
That night, they set the gifts on the bench.
Then they hid to watch.
***
At midnight, the elves came in.
They saw the tiny clothes.
"Are these for us?" they asked.
They put them on.
"Look at us!" they sang.
They danced all over the room.
Then they danced out the door.
The shoemaker and his wife smiled.
When someone is kind to you, say thank you.

cards.q: Who made the shoes at night?
cards.note: The shoemaker and his wife hid and saw them come in at midnight.

cards.q: Where did the shoemaker set the leather?
cards.note: A shoemaker works at a bench, a strong table for cutting and sewing.

cards.q: What was the big surprise in the morning?
cards.note: Every stitch neat and tiny, and nobody saw who did it.

cards.q: What did the shoemaker and his wife make for the elves?
cards.note: Tiny shirts, tiny coats and two pairs of tiny shoes, because the elves looked so cold.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: One last bit of leather, cut out and left on the bench: that is where it all starts.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: Warm at last, the elves danced right out the door.

cards.q: How did the elves feel in their new clothes?
cards.note: They sang and danced: the story shows it without saying the word.
When someone is kind to you, say thank you; the tiny clothes were the shoemaker's thank-you.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'midnight' mean?
cards.note: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night, the middle of the night, when everyone is asleep.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
